(A) NOT translation: B60DDF84 (the shader we 'fixed' for the logo) is NEVER bound at any real draw (0/3830 FM2_LIVE_PS; only CreateShader + PROBE). Its fork translation is byte-identical to clean upstream hedge-dev XenosRecomp (diff exit 0). (B) NOT binding: the logo is actually drawn by 9E93B374 (guest PS obj 0x4005D1B0) -- the SAME 8-stage material shader that already renders the textured background -- and its real art is correctly bound: the logo-banner art at guest base 0x10540000 (877x188, cls=VARIED real content, bc=1, fetch-constant-translated NOT aperture) sits in sampler slot 0 for those draws (FM2_LIVE_PS n=9/12/15 ps=0x4005D1B0 + FM2_LIVE_TEX slot=0 base=0x10540000 tex=..44230 bc=1). So shader+texture are both correct. 9E93B374 is FM2's shared material shader drawing bg+logo+A-button, each its own draw with its own texture and PER-DRAW constants; the bg draws show textured while the logo draw is black WITH THE SAME SHADER AND CORRECT ART => the blackness is per-draw STATE: the 8-stage blend leans on PS float constants (g_ColorTextureStages / c254 / c255 / g_Material) and g_Booleans stage gating. Aperture red herring: the fmt=24 1280x720 uniform-black surfaces (0x0A018000 etc.) sampled by A4AF88D4/composite passes ARE genuinely-empty resolve RTs (guest memory itself is uniform 000000FF, so translating the fetch gives black too) -- that is the separate scene/resolve-RT-black problem, not this logo.
bugs.fix: DIAGNOSED via two runtime instrumentation passes (FM2_MATCONST in d3d_hooks ApplyLivePixelShaderFromContext; FM2_PSUPLOAD at the render_state.cpp constant-upload site). AUTHORITATIVE RESULT for the logo draw (tex0 ptr correlated to FM2_LIVE_TEX base=0x10540000): post-PM4-merge g_ColorTextureStages(0)=PS[6]=[1.000,1.000,0.000,0.000] (texture weight .x=1 => TEXTURE ENABLED), merged=0 (PM4 overlay did NOT drop/replace it), colorWrite=0xF (all channels on), RT=0x130C41000 1280x720 (valid), blend=alpha-over (src=5 SRC_ALPHA, dst=6 INV_SRC_ALPHA). EVERY measurable pipeline input is correct => RULES OUT six subsystems: XenosRecomp translation, texture binding, color constants, colorWrite, render target, blend state. NOTE on the earlier 'constants zero' scare: the first FM2_MATCONST read the game register file at ctx+0x1710 but the shader's PS constants upload from ctx+0x1700 (psConstSrc, register N at byte N*16) -- a one-register shift; corrected, constants are FINE. bugs.error_message: RenderDoc CORE BUG (not renderdoc-mcp) FIXED + rebuilt + verified: get_shader/DisassembleShader returned 'Invalid Shader Specified' for every shader in fm2menunocar.rdc
bugs.root_cause: Traced end-to-end via a standalone python script against the renderdoc pymodules (bypassing the MCP layer) to walk the capture's full chunk list + call the replay API directly. D3D12Replay::GetShader() (d3d12_replay.cpp:542) correctly finds the ShaderEntry by resourceId, then returns &sh->GetDetails(). ShaderEntry::GetDetails() (d3d12_resources.h ~1005) sets m_Built=true UNCONDITIONALLY after attempting BuildReflection(), even if BuildReflection() never ran (GetDXBC()==NULL) or threw partway through MakeShaderReflection() -- for this shader's DXC-linker-produced DXIL container (missing PSV0/ISG1/OSG1, a known project finding). ShaderReflection::resourceId is ONLY ever assigned inside BuildReflection() (d3d12_resources.cpp:637, m_Details->resourceId = GetResourceID()), which runs AFTER the (failing) reflection-parse call -- so on failure resourceId stays at its default/invalid ResourceId(). This gets latched forever (m_Built never resets, no retry). DisassembleShader() then does GetResAs<WrappedID3D12Shader>(refl->resourceId) with that invalid id and correctly returns null -> the sentinel. The actual ShaderEntry/bytecode was NEVER missing or unregistered -- confirmed via raw structured-chunk inspection (Device_CreateGraphicsPipeline chunk present, InlineShaderIDs correctly wired to 10567/10568, VS BytecodeLength=6676 real bytes) -- only the REFLECTION OBJECT never got linked back to it.
bugs.fix: One-line fix: set `m_Details->resourceId = GetResourceID();` unconditionally in the ShaderEntry constructor (right after `m_Details = new ShaderReflection;`, d3d12_resources.h ~line 890), instead of relying solely on the assignment inside BuildReflection() which may never run. VERIFIED: rebuilt full renderdoc.sln (renderdoc.dll + pymodules/renderdoc.pyd) and re-ran the same standalone script against fm2menunocar.rdc -- refl.resourceId now correctly equals the bound shader id (10567), and DisassembleShader returns real ~10.8KB DXIL disassembly instead of the sentinel. Regression-checked fm2mainmenucorrect.rdc (event 61, VS 545) still disassembles fine (69KB DXBC text, unchanged). NOT YET committed to the renderdoc repo (user hasn't asked).

bugs.error_message: RenderDoc full-solution build failed with a chain of environment/toolset issues before it would even compile
bugs.root_cause: Three stacked issues in this Claude shell environment: (1) git-bash mangles MSBuild's /switch args into POSIX paths (e.g. /t:Build -> t:Build) -- must invoke MSBuild from the PowerShell tool, not Bash. (2) A plain shell here has a stale VS2022-era INCLUDE/LIB already set (same root cause as [[project_fm2_build_lib_env]]) that breaks vcvarsall.bat's setup unless explicitly cleared (`set INCLUDE=` / `set LIB=` / `set LIBPATH=`) before calling it, in a .bat file (not inline via nested cmd /c quoting, which mangles paths). (3) Independent of the env issue: several legacy sub-projects (ARM.vcxproj, renderdoc_dxgi/spirv/dxil, renderdocui_stub) hardcode `<PlatformToolset>v140</PlatformToolset>` (VS2015) which isn't installed alongside the VS18 toolset actually present -- passing `/p:PlatformToolset=v145` on the MSBuild command line overrides it (command-line global properties beat plain PropertyGroup assignments in the vcxproj). Also: building a single .vcxproj directly (not via renderdoc.sln) breaks because renderdoc.vcxproj imports `$(SolutionDir)\util\WindowsSDKTarget.props`, and SolutionDir is empty outside a solution build -- must build via renderdoc.sln, not the individual project file.
bugs.fix: Working recipe: write a .bat file that (a) clears INCLUDE/LIB/LIBPATH and sets a minimal PATH, (b) calls vcvars64.bat, (c) runs `MSBuild.exe renderdoc.sln /t:Build /m /nologo /verbosity:minimal /p:Configuration=Development /p:Platform=x64 /p:PlatformToolset=v145` -- then invoke that .bat via `cmd /c` from the PowerShell tool (not Bash) with output redirected to a log file, run in background (full build ~5-10 min). Confirmed working end-to-end: rebuilt renderdoc.dll + pymodules/renderdoc.pyd + qrenderdoc.exe successfully this way.
